sentences.text: Eremosuchus is an extinct animal belonging to the sebecosuchian group of notosuchians.
The type species for this genus is E. elkoholicus; it is currently placed within the family Sebecosuchia, whereas it was originally assigned to the family Trematochampsidae in 1989.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a slender lower jaw bone measuring 156 mm in total length.
This jaw contains twelve tooth sockets arranged in a full row, with the front teeth angled forward due to the orientation of their sockets.
A unique feature of this skeleton is that the lower half of the fibula curves backward, a trait not seen in other related crocodylomorphs.
The vertebrae are amphicoelous, meaning they are concave on both ends, with dorsal vertebrae showing a rounded bottom edge and noticeable narrowing.
Additionally, the tail vertebrae display prominent parallel ridges on the underside that cover about one-third of the centrum's length.
The animal possessed serrated, blade-like teeth known as ziphodonty, suggesting a specialized way of processing food.
Juvenile specimens show a lower jaw that diverged at an angle of 15 to 20 degrees, whereas the adult jaw diverged at an angle of 10 to 15 degrees.
Isolated osteoderms found at the site may have belonged to Eremosuchus, though experts debate whether multiple ornamentation types belong to this species or if neither type does.
Fossil remains were recovered in 1982 at the El Kohol site in northern Algeria by researchers from the Université d'Oran, Sorbonne Universités, and Université de Montpellier.
The genus was first described in 1989 based on isolated cranial and postcranial material.
Cecily S. C. Nicholl and colleagues published a redescription of the animal in 2025.
Changes in tooth shape from juvenile to adult may reflect a change in feeding strategy.
The gap between the seventh and eighth dentary teeth in the juvenile specimen might be a distinguishing feature shared with other species or simply intraspecific variation.
Researchers question whether tooth diameter is a reliable indicator of tooth size due to the poor preservation of the holotype.
Eremosuchus is currently the only named sebecid known from Africa and may link South American and European taxa.
In 1989, Eric Buffetaut originally assigned the genus to the family Trematochampsidae, a classification that Turner and Calvo later questioned.
Eremosuchus lived during the Ypresian stage of the Early Eocene, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
The environment where it lived was a shallow lake subject to periodic drying and occasional high-energy water inflows.
It is debated whether Eremosuchus's lineage split off during sebecid dispersal between South America and Europe, or if ancestors arrived in North Africa from Europe via the Tethys Sea.
Turner and Calvo argued that the features used to assign Eremosuchus to Trematochampsidae were of questionable value.
